newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on U.S. long bond dip.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on U.S. long bond dip.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 40 basis points at 20.80 percent on Friday after foreign traders switched from the U.S. bond market, traders said.
"They (foreign investors) sought better returns, especially after long bond rates fell," one trader said.

Yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds fell in early trade to 6.68 percent from 6.76 percent in late trade on Thursday, following the release of U.S. employment data, but then increased to 6.71 percent.
The late increase in long bond yields was matched by overnight Cetes rates, which closed above a session low of 21.40 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper ended down 40 basis points at 22.35 percent.
Traders said foreign investment inflows could be seen in a strong performance by the peso. Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 1.55 centavos firmer at 7.8050/7.8080 per dollar.
Banco de Mexico drained 1.807 billion pesos in liquidity from the market through three auctions to purchase paper.
Traders said the firm peso and a slight downward trend in secondary rates set the stage for further cuts in primary rates at next Tuesday's auction.
Dealers saw bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury Certificates) rates falling by some 25 basis points from last week's assignment rate of 21.45 percent.
Traders said that inflation figures announced came too late to have any effect on trade, but were in line with expectations and would thus support forecasts of cuts in primary rates.
The central bank announced that the Consumer Price Index rose 2.57 percent in January, compared to 3.20 percent in December.
A Reuters survey MXAAP of nine financial houses in Mexico City had predicted an average figure of 2.4 percent.
Liquidity of 307 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Monday.
